```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

TRSC's pre-treatment projection does not imply a causal bridge. This guide
maintains the untreated conditional-mean bridge and declared continuation
restrictions. It concerns identified sets, not realized missing outcomes.

```{r}
library(TRSC)
g <- trsc_geometry(matrix(c(0, 0, 1), 1,
                         dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "B", "C"))))
x <- c(A = 0, B = 2, C = 1)
fiber <- trsc_evaluation_set(g, x, representative = c(A = 1, B = 0, C = 0))
fiber
trsc_evaluation_width(fiber)
trsc_point_identified(fiber)
```

Donors A and B are predictively identical, but deployment distinguishes them.
Fixing the profile leaves the evaluation interval [0,2]. Compatible numerical
lifts are retained, with feasibility diagnostics in each optimization result.

```{r}
z <- trsc_counterfactual_set(g, rbind(x, x), c(A = 1, B = 0, C = 0),
                            q = 1, R = 0)
trsc_bounds(z)
trsc_support(z, c(1, -1))
```

The object is a plug-in set because the supplied inputs have not been
certified as population inputs. The coordinates in `trsc_bounds()` form a
rectangle enclosing projections; the lazy support oracle retains the actual
joint restrictions.

## A measurement must use the same latent witness

Suppose a treatment-unaffected auxiliary measurement equals the same response
functional here and its observed value is exactly 0.5 at each date. This is a
toy exact measurement law, not a use of a noisy observation as a mean.

```{r}
refined <- trsc_auxiliary_refine(z,
  maps = list(matrix(x, 1), matrix(x, 1)), values = list(.5, .5),
  source = "Toy shared composition; known response and exact treatment exclusion")
trsc_bounds(refined)
```

The constraints act on the same future weights as the continuation program.
Donor identity matters in the augmented experiment. Duplicating all predictive,
deployment and auxiliary characteristics preserves the set; duplicating only
predictive characteristics can introduce genuine evaluation ambiguity.
